title: Rule catalogue management
summary: Management layer on top of the QS-112 rule pool, QS-113 analyzer rules and QS-114 metrics. Recommends a host-level catalogue workspace (option B) over the existing files: rule lifecycle in frontmatter (proposed, active, deprecated, retired via enabled:false), named profiles as a host layer assigned per repository, overrides with lapsing expiry, a finding-effect preview that waives open findings with a traceable retirement marker whenever a rule is turned off, governance on the existing repository-client and registrar privileges with Git review for project scope and snapshots for global scope, and metric signals (noisy, contested, silent) that feed a rule health queue without retiring rules automatically. States that QS-112 and QS-113 are not yet on main and QS-114 has no delivery, and cuts the work into eight cards over two waves.

implementationTasks.title: Rule catalogue browser across repositories
implementationTasks.acceptanceScope: Read-only host catalogue view and its aggregate endpoint; no write paths.
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
Implement card 1 (wave 1) from docs/rule-catalogue-management/index.html.

Prerequisite: QS-112 (rule pool v1) and QS-113 (analyzer rules) are on main, with the shared rule library version resolved. Use the working decisions in docs/rule-catalogue-management/index.html unless the Dossier records another operator decision, and record which option you implemented.

**Build**
- `GET /api/rule-catalogue` (host level): resolve the pool of every registration the client may reach through the existing `RulePoolStore`/`ResolvedRuleCatalogue` cache. Return one entry per rule id with definition summary, `origin` (built-in, custom, imported once card 4 adds `importedFrom`), `enforcement` (`analyzer+agent` when `deterministicRuleIds` is non-empty, else `agent`), selecting packs, and per repository: enabled, effective severity, override scope and reason. Filters: `q` (id, title, statement, analyzer ids, case-insensitive, trailing-`*` families as in `DeterministicRuleMap`), technology, kind, origin, enforcement.
- Repositories with an invalid pool are listed with their diagnostics and do not fail the endpoint. Unreachable repositories are not disclosed.
- A host-level Rule catalogue view (shell entry next to Review policy) with search, facets, the table and a rule detail pane (statement, rationale, examples, change history, packs, repository matrix), following the "Browse and search" layout. Add a link to it from the QS-112 manager.

**Acceptance criteria**
1. Searching `CA2016` returns QS-CS-003. Searching `TS2322` returns QS-NG-014 through its `TS*` family.
2. With two registrations, one with an override, the matrix shows each repository's state and the override reason. A client limited to one repository sees only that one.
3. A registration whose `overrides.json` names an unknown rule appears with its located diagnostic, and the others still load.
4. API tests for filters, access scoping and invalid pools. Component tests for search and facets. Light and dark screenshots of the view against a real build.
5. No write route is added and no rule file changes.

implementationTasks.title: Rule lifecycle status, deprecation and pilots
implementationTasks.acceptanceScope: Lifecycle fields in rule format, schemas, resolution and UI; built-in library tooling.
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
Implement card 2 (wave 1) from docs/rule-catalogue-management/index.html.

Prerequisite: QS-112 (rule pool v1) and QS-113 (analyzer rules) are on main, with the shared rule library version resolved. Use the working decisions in docs/rule-catalogue-management/index.html unless the Dossier records another operator decision, and record which option you implemented. Card 1 must exist.

**Build**
- Optional rule frontmatter `status: proposed | active | deprecated` (default active), `sunset` (date, required when deprecated), `replacedBy` (a rule id that must resolve). `enabled: false` keeps meaning retired and wins over status. Add the fields to `rule-catalogue.v1` entries (additive), `RuleMarkdown`, `scripts/sync-rule-catalogue.mjs` validation and the rule template.
- Resolution: no pack selector selects a proposed rule, including an explicit `ids` selector. An override with `enabled: true` may enable it (pilot). Status is not prompt text: the effective input hash is unchanged by a status change, so a status change causes no policy drift.
- A status transition requires a version bump and a new change-history entry. Validation rejects a missing sunset, an unknown `replacedBy` or a missing history entry, with located diagnostics.
- UI: status badge and sunset in the catalogue and on rule cards. Deprecate and activate actions for custom rules in their owning scope (they edit the rule through `PUT /rules/custom/{ruleId}` with a reason). For built-in rules, "Retire on this host" writes a global `enabled: false` override (registrar only), shown as "Retired here". A "Library changed" note shows rules added, deprecated or retired when `catalogueVersion` differs from the last version this host has seen.

**Acceptance criteria**
1. A proposed custom rule selected by a `technologies` pack selector does not reach a review prompt. With a pilot override it does.
2. Changing only `status` leaves stored review sidecars without policy drift. A test proves the effective input hash is unchanged.
3. A deprecated rule without `sunset` makes the pool invalid with a located diagnostic. Its sunset passing changes no behaviour.
4. `npm run rules:check` and the catalogue tests cover the new fields. Existing rules without the fields resolve as before.
5. Light and dark screenshots of the badges and the deprecate dialog.

implementationTasks.title: Rule overrides with expiry
implementationTasks.acceptanceScope: expiresAt on overrides: schema, resolution, cache keys, editor UI and expiry listing.
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
Implement card 3 (wave 1) from docs/rule-catalogue-management/index.html.

Prerequisite: QS-112 (rule pool v1) and QS-113 (analyzer rules) are on main, with the shared rule library version resolved. Use the working decisions in docs/rule-catalogue-management/index.html unless the Dossier records another operator decision, and record which option you implemented. Card 1 must exist.

**Build**
- Optional `expiresAt` (UTC date-time) on the `rule-config.v1` override, accepted by `PUT /rules/overrides/{ruleId}`, carried in `rule-set.v1` and `rule-audit.v1` before and after. A write with a past `expiresAt` is rejected with 400.
- Resolution ignores an expired override: the rule falls back to the lower layers, and a warning diagnostic (not an error) names the override and its expiry. Reviews keep running.
- The pool cache and the hierarchy snapshot key include the set of currently active overrides (or the next expiry instant), so a lapse becomes effective without any file change.
- UI: the override editor gains an Expires field. For a disable or a severity downgrade it defaults to 90 days, and "No expiry" must be chosen explicitly. The catalogue shows an expiring marker (within 14 days) and a count of permanent overrides, and lists expired overrides so they can be removed or renewed.

**Acceptance criteria**
1. With a clock seam, an override that expires between two requests stops applying on the second. The rule's effective state and the tree ETag change without any file write.
2. An expired override yields a warning diagnostic. `valid` stays true and a review runs.
3. Existing overrides without `expiresAt` behave exactly as before, and export/import round-trips the field.
4. Unit, API and component tests. Light and dark screenshots of the editor with its default expiry.

implementationTasks.title: Pack composer and pack import from another repository
implementationTasks.acceptanceScope: Pack editor with preview and impact, version enforcement, single-pack export closure and import, importedFrom marker.
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
Implement card 4 (wave 1) from docs/rule-catalogue-management/index.html.

Prerequisite: QS-112 (rule pool v1) and QS-113 (analyzer rules) are on main, with the shared rule library version resolved. Use the working decisions in docs/rule-catalogue-management/index.html unless the Dossier records another operator decision, and record which option you implemented. Card 1 must exist.

**Build**
- Pack composer over `rule-pack.v1` in the catalogue view: selector rows (ids, technologies, kinds, categories, defaultOn), live preview of selected rules resolved against the target scope's pool (proposed rules shown as skipped once card 2 exists), and impact per using repository (rules gained or lost, unit count that will show policy drift) from a dry-run resolution. Save through `PUT /rules/packs/{packId}` with a reason.
- If the selection changes, `version` must change: the server rejects a changed selection with an unchanged version. The UI suggests minor when the selection widens and major when it narrows.
- `GET /rules/export?pack=<id>` returns a `rule-set.v1` holding only that pack plus the custom rules its `ids` selectors need that the pack's scope defines (closure). No applicability or overrides.
- Import-pack flow: choose a source registration, scope and pack. The target is the current repository or global. Run `POST /rules/import` in merge mode as a dry run, show added, unchanged and conflicting entries (a conflicting custom rule defaults to keeping the target's copy), then apply with a reason. The client must reach both repositories.
- Optional `importedFrom` { name, repository, digest, at } on custom rules (frontmatter) and packs (additive schema fields), written by import and read as the Imported origin in the catalogue.

**Acceptance criteria**
1. Importing a pack that selects `ids: [ACME-CS-004]` into a repository without that rule adds the pack and the rule, leaves applicability and overrides unchanged, and writes one `rule-set.import` audit line.
2. A conflicting custom rule is not overwritten by default, and the dry run lists it as a conflict.
3. Saving a changed selection with the same version returns 400 with a diagnostic.
4. API tests for closure, access to both repositories, and conflicts. A browser flow with light and dark screenshots of composer and import preview.

implementationTasks.title: Named rule profiles assigned per repository
implementationTasks.acceptanceScope: rule-profile.v1, profile layer in resolution, registration assignment, profile screens with dry-run impact.
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
Implement card 5 (wave 2) from docs/rule-catalogue-management/index.html.

Prerequisite: QS-112 (rule pool v1) and QS-113 (analyzer rules) are on main, with the shared rule library version resolved. Use the working decisions in docs/rule-catalogue-management/index.html unless the Dossier records another operator decision, and record which option you implemented. Cards 1 and 3 must exist.

**Build**
- New schema `rule-profile.v1`: id, version, title, description, packs[], overrides[] (the `rule-config.v1` override shape including `expiresAt`), stored as `<data root>/rules/profiles/<id>.json`. A profile references packs and rules and never defines rules.
- Registration field `ruleProfile` { id, reason }, set via a registrar-only route. Resolution gains a profile layer. Applicability order: project, profile, global, house-style. Override order: global, shared global inputs, profile, project. An unknown profile id makes the pool invalid (fail closed, located diagnostic).
- Routes: list, get, put and delete profiles (registrar only, reason required, version must change when content changes). Assign and unassign a profile with `dryRun`, returning rules enabled, disabled and re-severitied, units that will show policy drift, and project-scope settings that will keep winning.
- UI: the Repositories · rule profiles list and the Apply profile dialog as in the Dossier layout, including the "kept by project" warning.

**Acceptance criteria**
1. A repository without project applicability that is assigned a profile with packs `[dotnet-service]` resolves exactly those packs. With a project `applicability.json` the project wins, and the dry run says so.
2. A profile override applies below project overrides and above global ones. Tests cover every layer order.
3. A non-registrar client gets 403 on profile writes and assignment.
4. The profile file set is part of the pool fingerprint, so editing a profile refreshes the tree of every assigned repository.
5. API, resolution and component tests. Light and dark screenshots of the list and the dialog.

implementationTasks.title: Host-wide rule audit timeline and global history
implementationTasks.acceptanceScope: Cross-scope audit read API and view, derived lapse and outside-edit rows, global snapshots and restore, uncommitted flag.
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
Implement card 6 (wave 2) from docs/rule-catalogue-management/index.html.

Prerequisite: QS-112 (rule pool v1) and QS-113 (analyzer rules) are on main, with the shared rule library version resolved. Use the working decisions in docs/rule-catalogue-management/index.html unless the Dossier records another operator decision, and record which option you implemented. Card 1 must exist.

**Build**
- `GET /api/rule-audit`: merge the global `audit.jsonl` (with rotated files) and every reachable project's audit into one timeline, newest first, with filters for scope, repository, action, rule or target, actor and time range, plus paging. Show stored `before` and `after` as a field diff in the view.
- Derived rows (not appended to the files): *override lapsed* for each expired `expiresAt` (card 3, if present), and *changed outside Quality Studio* when a scope's pool fingerprint changed without a matching audit line. The latter needs the last seen fingerprint per scope stored in the data root.
- On every accepted global write, store a `rule-set.v1` snapshot in `<data root>/rules/history/<utc>-<digest12>.json` and rotate after 200. Restore = `POST /rules/import` with `scope=global`, `mode=replace`, dry run shown first, registrar only.
- The catalogue marks repositories whose `.quality/rules` has uncommitted changes (read-only Git status), and review run records store the rule pool digest with a `ruleFilesUncommitted` flag.
- The audit view states that the actor is unauthenticated in Local mode.

**Acceptance criteria**
1. Two repositories and a global change appear in one timeline in order, and the filters narrow them correctly.
2. Editing `overrides.json` by hand produces one *changed outside Quality Studio* row and no duplicate on reload.
3. Restoring a snapshot as a dry run lists the changes. Applying it makes the global scope byte-equal to the snapshot content and writes one audit line.
4. A repository with an uncommitted `.quality/rules` change is flagged, and the next review run record carries the flag.
5. API and component tests. Light and dark screenshots.

implementationTasks.title: Turning a rule off with its effect on open findings
implementationTasks.acceptanceScope: Finding-effect preview and retirement waiver for every rule-off action; reopen on reactivation.
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
Implement card 7 (wave 2) from docs/rule-catalogue-management/index.html.

Prerequisite: QS-112 (rule pool v1) and QS-113 (analyzer rules) are on main, with the shared rule library version resolved. Use the working decisions in docs/rule-catalogue-management/index.html unless the Dossier records another operator decision, and record which option you implemented. Card 2 must exist.

**Build**
- A finding-effect preview for any change that turns a rule off in a scope: retire (custom `enabled: false` or built-in "Retire on this host"), a disable override, removing a rule from a pack, and (when card 5 exists) a profile assignment. For each affected repository, count findings with that `ruleId` by state from `findings/state.json` and sidecars, and show the effective-grade change.
- Options: open and not-reobserved findings are waived as retired (default on), accepted findings are kept (default), waived and false-positive findings are unchanged. Apply through `FindingStateStore.SetAsync` with state `waived`, author `rule-retirement:<ruleId>`, and the change's reason. Write one audit line summarising counts per repository.
- Reactivating the rule (enabled again, override removed, status back to active) offers to reopen exactly the findings whose author is `rule-retirement:<ruleId>`.
- The rule-off write and the finding step are separate operations. If the finding step fails in one repository, the rule change stands, the UI shows what remains, and the step can be retried idempotently.

**Acceptance criteria**
1. After retiring a rule with 3 open findings and re-reviewing the unit with changed code, those findings are `waived` and not `resolved`. The grade excludes their deficit and they stay visible.
2. Accepted findings keep their state unless the operator opts in.
3. Reactivation offers the reopen step, and it reopens only the marked findings.
4. Retirement waivers are excluded from the Dismissed measure.
5. Tests for merge interaction, idempotent retry and access scoping. Light and dark screenshots of the dialog.

implementationTasks.title: Rule health from effectiveness metrics
implementationTasks.acceptanceScope: Metrics columns and detail in the catalogue, three retirement signals, rule health queue with audited actions.
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
Implement card 8 (wave 2) from docs/rule-catalogue-management/index.html.

Prerequisite: QS-112 (rule pool v1) and QS-113 (analyzer rules) are on main, with the shared rule library version resolved. Use the working decisions in docs/rule-catalogue-management/index.html unless the Dossier records another operator decision, and record which option you implemented. Card 7 and QS-114's effectiveness metrics must exist. If QS-114's API differs from the Dossier's metrics contract, adapt to QS-114 and note the mapping.

**Build**
- Catalogue columns and rule detail: hits (agent) and analyzer hits, accepted, dismissed (waived + false-positive, excluding `rule-retirement:*` authors), false positives, false-positive rate with its denominator n, and resolved, over 30, 90 and 180 days, per repository and in total.
- Signals with host-configurable thresholds and defaults from the Dossier. Noisy: false-positive rate ≥ 40 % with n ≥ 20 in 90 days. Contested: disabled or downgraded in ≥ 50 % of at least 4 selecting repositories. Silent: no hits for 180 days while active in ≥ 3 repositories. Also list *sunset passed* for deprecated rules.
- A Rule health queue with the actions keep (snooze one window), rewrite (open the custom rule editor, or record a library note for built-in rules), deprecate (card 2) and retire (card 7). Each action needs a reason and writes an audit line. No signal changes a rule by itself.

**Acceptance criteria**
1. With fixture state (25 dispositioned findings, 11 false positives in 90 days), the rule shows 44 % FP at n = 25 and appears as Noisy. With n = 19 it does not.
2. A retirement-waived finding does not count as dismissed.
3. Keep snoozes the item for exactly one window, and the audit records it.
4. Unit tests for every measure and signal boundary. Light and dark screenshots of the queue and the metrics columns.
